stem:
Mona watches the Sun after sunrise. It climbs, then later sinks toward the west.

Why does the Sun appear to move from east to west?

options.text: Earth rotates from west to east on its own axis.
Earth revolves around the Sun once each year.
Earth rotates from east to west on its own axis.
Earth's rotation explains the Moon's path, not the Sun's.

teacher.key_rationale: The Sun's apparent east-to-west path comes from Earth's west-to-east rotation on its axis. Yearly revolution is a different motion. East-to-west rotation reverses the direction. Rotation also explains the Sun's daily path, not only the Moon's.
